text:
sam: Heads-up — saw a small surge of duplicate downstream calls from the onboarding sample app during a token rotation window, ended up with a bunch of 429s and retries firing in quick succession.

anya: Ack. Any logs/stack traces? Is this the client or our proxy layering retries?

sam: Quick paste of the request flow from the sample app logs:
```
INFO 2026-06-01T12:00:10Z outgoing request id=abc123 auth=Bearer old_token
INFO 2026-06-01T12:00:11Z token rotated -> new_token
WARN 2026-06-01T12:00:11Z request id=abc123 retried due to 401, retry_count=1
INFO 2026-06-01T12:00:12Z outgoing request id=abc123 auth=Bearer new_token
ERROR 2026-06-01T12:00:12Z upstream returned 429 for request id=abc123
INFO 2026-06-01T12:00:12Z client retried immediately without jitter -> duplicate side-effect observed
```

marta: Oof — looks like the client is re-issuing the same logical call right after refresh, resetting the backoff. We intentionally wanted the SDK to treat token-refresh retries as part of the existing retry window, not restart it.

raj: That matches an old parity bug I saw in the JS SDK: when `onAuthRefresh` resolves, it resets the exponential backoff state. Python kept the backoff counter intact, but JS clears it. Could cause tight retry loops across many clients during a rotation.

sam: Repro steps I used: run sample app with a short token TTL (5s) and a simulated auth server that rotates token, then spike a few requests. You can reproduce with the `sample-onboard` repo.

anya: For mitigation, can we do two things quickly: 1) ensure the SDK doesn't zero the backoff on token refresh (parity fix), and 2) add small randomized jitter on immediate retry after auth refresh (e.g., 50-150ms) to spread retries?

marta: Agreed. Also recommend a guard in the sample app to attach an `Idempotency-Key` header for operations that are not strictly idempotent — helps server-side dedupe if duplicate hits happen.

raj: Note: server dedupe requires that downstream handlers are idempotency-aware; not all onboarding flows are. But adding the header is low-cost and a helpful hint.

sam: Would a short-term server fallback help? E.g., when we detect surge + token rotation, route to a lower-throughput bucket or return a 503 so clients back off?

marta: We have routing policies but automatic fallback might be too heavy for onboarding. I'd prefer SDK-first mitigations and a quick patch to the sample app docs to highlight token rotation test caveats.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: JS SDK fix candidate branch "fix/auth-backoff-reset" will be deployed to staging at 2026-06-01T12:10Z.

anya: Thanks — can someone open a small triage ticket with repro steps + link to sample app and mark as P2? I'll coordinate a short doc update and a small test in the CI harness to simulate token rotation.

sam: Filed: https://redwood-internal/issues/INFR-8421 (includes logs and repro script). I'll add a tiny harness test to the sample app.

marta: Nice. Post-deploy, let's run the 100-client rotation test overnight and check if 429 spike disappears. :crossed_fingers:

raj: I'll add a unit test in the JS SDK asserting the backoff counter is preserved across `onAuthRefresh`.

sam: Thanks all — will update here after staging run.
